prompt: Two angles of a triangle measure $40^\circ$ and $75^\circ$. What is the third angle, in degrees?
hint: The three angles of ANY triangle always add to $180^\circ$.

hints.text: The three angles of ANY triangle always add to $180^\circ$.
First add what you know: $40 + 75 = 115$. Then see what is missing from $180$.

explanation: The three angles of every triangle add up to $180^\circ$.
The two known angles use up $40 + 75 = 115$ degrees of that total.
The third angle is what remains: $180 - 115 = 65$ degrees.

alternativeExplanations.title: Tear the corners off
steps: Imagine tearing the three corners off a paper triangle and placing them side by side.
The three corners always fit together into a straight line, and a straight line measures $180^\circ$.
The corners of $40^\circ$ and $75^\circ$ fill $115^\circ$ of that line, so the missing corner is $180 - 115 = 65$ degrees.

alternativeExplanations.title: Subtract one angle at a time
steps: Start with the full $180^\circ$ and take away the first known angle: $180 - 40 = 140$.
Take away the second known angle from what is left: $140 - 75 = 65$.
Nothing else remains to subtract, so the third angle is $65^\circ$.
